title: Meet middle C
summary: Find your way around the keys and play C, D and E with fingers 1, 2 and 3.
goals: Read C, D and E on the treble staff

steps.title: Groups of two and three
steps.body: Black keys come in groups of two and three. Every C is the white key just left of a group of two. Middle C is the C closest to the middle of your keyboard, often near the brand name.

steps.title: Your right-hand fingers have numbers
steps.body: Thumb is 1, index 2, middle 3, ring 4, little finger 5. Rest your thumb on middle C and let fingers 2 and 3 fall on D and E.

steps.title: On the staff
steps.body: Middle C sits on its own short line below the treble staff. D hangs just under the bottom line. E sits on the bottom line. The music waits for you, so take your time.

title: Five fingers in C position
summary: Put all five right-hand fingers on C D E F G and play up, down and in skips.
goals: Keep each finger over its own key

steps.title: C position
steps.body: Thumb on middle C, then one finger per white key: C D E F G under fingers 1 2 3 4 5. Keep your hand curved, as if holding a ball.

steps.title: Steps and skips
steps.body: Moving to the next key is a step (line to space on the staff). Jumping over a key is a skip (line to line). Bar 5 skips C–E–G.

title: The left hand joins
summary: Play the same five notes an octave lower with the left hand, reading the bass staff.
goals: Find the C below middle C
Read C to G on the bass staff

steps.title: Left-hand C position
steps.body: Left-hand fingers are numbered from the thumb too, so the little finger (5) plays the low C and the thumb (1) plays G.

steps.title: The bass staff
steps.body: The bass clef's two dots surround the F line. The C an octave below middle C sits in the second space from the bottom; G sits on the top line.

title: Whole, half and quarter notes
summary: Count steady beats and hold notes for their full length in Hot Cross Buns.
goals: Play in time with the metronome

steps.title: Note lengths
steps.body: A quarter note gets one beat, a half note two, a whole note four. Count “1 2 3 4” out loud with the clicks and keep holding a key until its beat is over.

steps.title: Playing in time
steps.body: From now on the music keeps going. Notes within 40 ms of the beat score Perfect, within 90 ms Good. The metronome clicks every beat; a one-bar count-in starts each run.

license.attribution: Hot Cross Buns: traditional melody, public domain. Arrangement written for Playboard.

title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
summary: A whole song in C position: keep the beat steady through repeated notes.

steps.title: Repeated notes
steps.body: Bars 2 and 6 repeat the same key. Let the key come up between notes so each one sounds, and keep them all the same loudness.

license.attribution: Mary Had a Little Lamb: traditional melody, public domain. Arrangement written for Playboard.

title: Ode to Joy, right hand
summary: Beethoven's famous theme with a dotted rhythm, while Playboard plays the left hand.
goals: Play a dotted quarter and eighth

steps.title: Dotted rhythm
steps.body: A dot adds half the note's value: a dotted quarter lasts one and a half beats, and the eighth note after it fills the last half beat. Bar 4 goes “long – short – hold”.

steps.title: Bar 12
steps.body: The right hand rests while the left-hand thumb plays a low G. Keep counting through the rest.

license.attribution: Ludwig van Beethoven, Symphony No. 9 (1824), public domain. Arrangement written for Playboard.

title: Hands together: Lightly Row
summary: Play a melody with the right hand while the left hand holds long bass notes.
goals: Hold the left hand while the right moves
Keep both hands in C position

steps.title: One hand moves, one holds
steps.body: The left hand plays one note per bar and holds it. Press both hands together on beat 1, then let the right hand carry on. Practise each hand alone first if it feels busy: choose Right or Left above the stage.

steps.title: Left-hand notes
steps.body: Only three left-hand notes: C (5), E (3) and G (1).

license.attribution: Lightly Row (Hänschen klein): traditional melody, public domain. Arrangement written for Playboard.

title: The C major scale
summary: Eight notes with five fingers: tuck the thumb under to keep going.
goals: Cross the thumb under after finger 3
Cross finger 3 over on the way down

steps.title: Thumb under
steps.body: Play C D E with 1 2 3, then slide the thumb under your hand to F and continue G A B C with 2 3 4 5. On the way down, finger 3 crosses over the thumb from F to E.

steps.title: Eighth notes
steps.body: Bar 5 plays two notes per beat. Count “1 and 2 and”. Start slowly with the tempo slider and speed up when it feels even.

title: First chords: C, F and G
summary: Three-note chords in the right hand, moving with as little motion as possible.
goals: Play three notes at exactly the same time
Move between C, F and G chords

steps.title: C chord
steps.body: C, E and G with fingers 1, 3 and 5.

steps.title: F chord, close to C
steps.body: Keep the thumb on C; finger 3 moves up to F and finger 5 to A.

steps.title: G chord, close to C
steps.body: Thumb steps down to B, finger 2 to D, finger 5 stays on G.

title: Hands together: Minuet in G
summary: A real Baroque dance for both hands, in G position and three-four time.
goals: Play eighth notes against a held bass
Play a 16-bar piece with both hands

steps.title: Three-four time
steps.body: A minuet is a dance in three: count “1 2 3” and lean slightly on beat 1. The left hand plays one dotted half note per bar, lasting all three beats.

steps.title: F sharp
steps.body: The sharp at the start of each staff means every F is played as F♯, the black key just right of F. You meet it in bars 3, 7 and 15.

steps.title: How to practise it
steps.body: Start at 70% tempo. Loop any bar that shows up in Weak spots, practise hands separately, then put them back together.

license.attribution: Christian Petzold, Minuet in G major, BWV Anh. 114 (c. 1725), public domain. Arrangement written for Playboard.
